baseline.workload: AC-3 geometry: the 10 pinned reference prompts (24-68 input tokens), 64 reported output tokens, one wave per process
baseline.measurement: megakernel profiler, 48M slots, 9.3-24.7M events/run, 3 reps per batch size; profiled vs unprofiled wave wall 2.85-3.59% apart; token ids byte-identical to the committed M2 report for all 25 (prompt,bs) cases

delta_model.note: expected_e2e_delta_per_bs is step_us/(step_us - recovered_wall_us) - 1 on the STEADY DECODE STEP, i.e. AC-4 decode throughput, unless the entry says wave-level. The wall-span decomposition is near-additive: the sum of per-task-type wall spans is 109-114% of the measured step at every batch size, so removing a stage's wall span is a defensible first-order model of the step it saves. Every number here is a HYPOTHESIS to be settled by the entry's verify_cmd, never acceptance (M3 milestone rules).

levers.evidence: 3840 tasks per step at EVERY batch size (grid_dim=(mbt,1,1), 96 per layer) -- the count is set by max_num_batched_tokens=16, not by live tokens, so total worker time is flat at 84.1/82.4/76.1 ms for bs1/4/16. Its wall footprint is the single largest of any task type at bs<=4: 4540 us of the 15264 us bs1 step (29.7%), 4244 us of the bs16 step (19.3%). Mean concurrency while it runs is only 33-35 of 128 blocks, and each task takes 19.8-21.9 us to block-quantize <=8 KB of activations -- three orders of magnitude off any bandwidth bound, i.e. pure launch/latency cost. Source: pertask_by_bs.csv rows TASK_QUANTIZE_FP8_SM100, tables/bs*_concurrency.json.
levers.mechanism: A separate task per (row, tensor) for a trivially cheap elementwise+reduction op. The producer (RMS-norm, SiLU-mul) already has the values in registers; quantizing in its epilogue removes both the task and the round trip through global memory.
levers.delta_basis: lower bound = half its wall span recovered, upper bound = all of it

levers.lever: Right-size MoE expert activation to the live token count
levers.evidence: The MoE GEMM grid is grid_x = min(num_experts, mbt*topk) = min(256,128) = 128 groups x moe_n_splits=2, fixed by mbt=16 -- independent of how many tokens are really in the step (builder.py:538). Measured live (>1 us) w13 tasks per layer: 112.7 at bs1, 118.8 at bs2, 120.4 at bs4, 140.2 at bs8, 173.3 at bs16 (of 256 launched), i.e. 56.4 / 59.4 / 60.2 / 70.1 / 86.7 active expert groups of 128. Top-8 routing on ONE token needs 8. So bs1 activates ~7x more experts -- and reads ~7x more expert weight -- than the routing requires; bs4 ~1.9x; bs16 is already right-sized. MoE w13+w2 wall span is 4786 us of the bs1 step (31%). Source: pertask_by_bs.csv nlong_bs* + wallspan_us_bs*.
levers.mechanism: The router (topk_softmax_sm100) routes all mbt=16 rows including the 15 phantom rows of a 1-token decode step; each phantom row contributes its own top-8 entries to moe_routing_indices/moe_mask, so the grouped GEMM streams those experts' weights for output that is then discarded.
levers.delta_basis: MoE wall span scaled by (1 - min(128, 8*bs)/measured_active_groups)
levers.risk: medium - touches the router. Phantom-row outputs are discarded, so this should be AC-3 neutral by construction, but it must be proven per-case, and MOE_ROUTER_MAX_ROWS_PER_TASK/the 16-row cap interact (M2-I9).

levers.evidence: worker-idle-while-others-work is 9.57/9.44/8.76/9.92/9.91 ms per step at bs 1/2/4/8/16 -- essentially BATCH-INDEPENDENT and 45-63% of every step. Mean concurrency is 43.5/46.5/51.9/55.2/68.3 of 128 blocks; 6.7-9.1 ms of every step runs at <=16 concurrent workers. It is not a dispatch-rate or stall problem: total all-idle (nobody in a task) is only 0.50 ms/step at every bs, workers take 332-475 inter-task gaps per step of mean 21-30 us and max 164 us. The low-concurrency stages are exactly the low-task-count ones: TASK_ATTN_SM100 2/layer -> concurrency 2.0 at bs1, TASK_GDN_CONV1D 8/layer -> 8.0, TASK_RMS_NORM/SIGMOID_GATE/MOE_MUL_SUM_ADD 16/layer -> 15-16, TASK_QUANTIZE_FP8 96/layer -> 34.6. Source: attribution.csv worker_idle_us + us_at_conc_le16, tables/bs*_concurrency.json per_task_concurrency.
levers.mechanism: MPK executes one CTA per task. A stage emitting 16 tasks occupies 16 of 148 SMs for its whole duration no matter how cheap it is, and the 40 layers are strictly sequential, so those stages stack up into a batch-independent floor.

levers.lever: Fix the mbt=16 admission policy: bs16 never reaches a decode steady state
levers.evidence: An exact replay of prepare_next_batch (opt/schedule_sim.py, validated against the trace's own BEGIN_TASK_GRAPH count at all five batch sizes: 109/109/109/111/203 predicted == observed) shows the bs16 wave spends 108 of 203 iterations in a MIXED prefill+decode regime and the other 95 draining, with ZERO iterations where all 16 requests decode. The first request retires at iteration 101 while another is still prefilling. Wave time splits 2754 ms mixed + 1920 ms drain of a 4695 ms wave. Cause: step 3 fills the 16-token budget greedily in slot order, so once the early slots are decoding they consume the whole budget and the late slots prefill one token at a time. Source: attribution.csv mixed_phase_*/drain_phase_*, tables/bs16_iters.csv.

new_levers_for_m4.lever: MPK prefill throughput at the 256/1024 workload
new_levers_for_m4.evidence: Measured directly for the first time: the prefill-only arm (same prompts, msl=259, n=3) costs 326/624/1190/2940/3041 ms at bs1/2/4/8/16 under the pinned policy = 3.2/5.8/10.3/20.4/20.0% of the whole 256/1024 e2e, rising to 29.2% at bs16 uncapped. The scale that matters is against the REFERENCE, not against ourselves: at bs8 MPK's prefill ALONE (2.94 s) is 59% of vLLM's entire end-to-end time (4.95 s), and at bs16 it is 55%. No M3 backlog item covers prefill: every M3 measurement was a decode step. opt/m3i7/tables/geomM_matched_256_1024.csv.
new_levers_for_m4.mechanism: mbt=16 caps the whole engine at 16 prefill tokens per iteration, so a 256-token prompt needs >=16 iterations and bs*256 tokens need bs*16 iterations at best -- and uncapped admission makes it far worse than that best case by serialising requests (lever 4's mechanism). vLLM prefills the same tokens in large fused chunks.
new_levers_for_m4.first_step: Extend the admission cap to bs4/bs8 (already measured, +3.9%/+14.0% e2e, AC-3 byte-identical), then attack mbt itself for the prefill phase only -- M3-I5b rejected raising mbt on DECODE evidence, which does not bind the prefill phase.
new_levers_for_m4.disposition: OPEN -> M4, ranked 1 by e2e effect

new_levers_for_m4.lever: Split-KV k-way attention (the I3 separate-task idiom applied to task 257)
new_levers_for_m4.found_by: M3-I6a, re-ranked by M3-I7 (milestone gate, 2026-07-29, integrated HEAD c80ebd68)
new_levers_for_m4.evidence: Attention is rank 5 in the re-derived table (4.50/4.63/4.98x vLLM, 501/518/628 us/step of gap) and it is the only target whose ratio GROWS with batch size. vLLM's own reference is a split-KV kernel (MultiCtasKv). I6a predicted 39 us vs 75 us at ctx 848, k=8.
new_levers_for_m4.mechanism: MPK runs 2 attention tasks per layer, so the stage occupies 2 of 148 SMs however long it takes; splitting the KV range k ways multiplies the available parallelism by k.
new_levers_for_m4.first_step: ferret task spec against the vLLM MultiCtasKv reference at ctx 848.

new_levers_for_m4.found_by: M3-I1, re-ranked by M3-I7 (milestone gate, 2026-07-29, integrated HEAD c80ebd68)
new_levers_for_m4.evidence: Ranks 1 and 3 in the re-derived table: w13 6.96/2.85/2.56x (2092/1847/2039 us/step of gap), w2 4.37/2.00/2.03x. Together they are ~3.2 ms of a 9.8 ms bs1 step. The bs1 ratio is far worse than bs8/bs16, which is the tensor-core-waste signature the ferret MoE task authoring already identified: BATCH_SIZE=16 is compile-fixed, so NUM_M_TILES=1 and every activated expert pays a full 16-row MMA tile (~94% waste at bs1).
new_levers_for_m4.mechanism: compile-fixed M tile vs live token count; distinct from lever 2, which fixed which experts are activated rather than what each costs.
new_levers_for_m4.first_step: the authored ferret MoE task (workspace3, launch line staged, target_ratio 1.3333) once the box quota resets.

new_levers_for_m4.evidence: Rank 4 and the biggest RATIO among the non-trivial stages: 5.70/4.93/4.12x vLLM, 731/770/801 us/step of gap, and it got WORSE relative to the previous table (3.36->5.70x at bs1) because the corrected window exposes it. 842-980 us/step for routing 1-16 tokens through a top-8-of-256 softmax is far above any plausible bound.
new_levers_for_m4.mechanism: not yet attributed. The stage was reshaped twice in M3 (I5b's row loop, I5c's compaction race fix, which cost +51-61% on the task by design) and has never had a kernel-level look.
new_levers_for_m4.first_step: attribute before optimising -- I5c knowingly traded speed for correctness here and that trade has never been re-costed.

new_levers_for_m4.lever: schedule_sim diverges from the runtime at bs16/msl=897
new_levers_for_m4.evidence: The exact-replay admission model predicts 1360 iterations; the trace has 1004. bs1 (656) and bs8 (810) match exactly. Anchor QC on that window fails (max_frac_err 0.4437 vs a 0.02 threshold, 16 task types mismatched), so bs16's per-stage row is flagged not-valid rather than used. opt/m3i7/stage/qc/anchor_qc_summary.json.
new_levers_for_m4.mechanism: unknown. It is a measurement-infrastructure defect, not a performance lever, but it blinds every bs16 per-stage number.
new_levers_for_m4.first_step: diff the replay against the runtime's own iteration labels at bs16/msl=897; the iters.csv the parse already writes has both.
new_levers_for_m4.disposition: OPEN -> M4 (blocks trustworthy bs16 stage attribution)

m4_ranking_notes.ranking_correction_20260729: M3 milestone review (first-principles) corrected the residual ranking: AC-4 measures STEADY-STATE DECODE throughput, so the decode-gap ranking governs it — MoE w13 (6.96x bs1), dense fp8 (2.07x, most batch-independent), MoE w2 (4.37x), MoE router (5.70x, regressed), graph width (why MPK is 2.25-2.79x off e2e while winning every fused stage). PREFILL IS AN AC-5 LEVER, NOT THE LEADING AC-4 ROUTE: extending the admission cap to bs4/bs8 (+3.9%/+14.0% e2e, AC-3 byte-identical) is the cheapest first AC-5 action and reduces the e2e ratio, but it does not move decode tok/s. The two tracks are now ranked SEPARATELY in the M4 plan.
